title: Use pasta for published-port forwarding on user-defined (bridge) networks, so that client source addresses are preserved
body:
### Feature request description

In rootless mode with a user-defined network, Podman already starts pasta to connect the rootless netns to the host - but explicitly disables its port forwarding (-t none -u none -T none -U none). Published ports are instead forwarded by rootlessport (rootlesskit), which SNATs the connection and therefore loses the client source address.

Since pasta is already running for exactly this netns, and preserving source addresses is one of its design goals: 
could the published-port forwarding be handed to pasta for bridge networks as well?

Current behaviour — Traefik rootless on a user-defined network, publishing 80/443. Its access log records the internal bridge address for a request that came from a public IPv4:
 {"ClientAddr":"10.89.1.7:57110","ClientHost":"10.89.1.7","RequestHost":"git.example.com","RequestMethod":"GET","DownstreamStatus":200,"RouterName":"gitea@file"}

pasta runs with forwarding off, rootlesskit does the work:

/usr/bin/pasta --config-net --pid …/rootless-netns-conn.pid --dns-forward 169.254.1.1 \
    -t none -u none -T none -U none --no-map-gw --quiet --netns …/rootless-netns \
    --map-guest-addr 169.254.1.2                                                                                                      

podmgr 44770  rootlessport
podmgr 44778  rootlessport-child                                                                                                    

This is not cosmetic for a reverse proxy. With every request appearing to come from one internal address:

- access logs cannot serve as an audit record - every request looks identical
- X-Forwarded-For set by the proxy carries the internal address, so all backends behind it inherit the wrong value
- per-client rate limiting silently becomes global rate limiting  
- authentication event logs (e.g. Keycloak login events) record the wrong IP                                                        
- fail2ban-style blocking is impossible, as there is nothing distinguishable to ban

The failure mode is silent: everything appears to work and the values are simply wrong.                                           



### Suggest potential solution

Hand published-port forwarding to pasta for user-defined networks as well, instead of using rootlesskit.

pasta is already running for the rootless netns and preserving source addresses is one of its design goals, so the mechanism is present - it is just started with -t none -u none -T none -U none and the ports are routed around it.

If replacing rootlesskit unconditionally is undesirable (rootlesskit is faster, which is presumably why it is the default), an opt-in would already help: a containers.conf setting, or extending the existing port_handler= option so that it also applies to netavark bridge networks rather than only to slirp4netns-backed ones.


### Have you considered any alternatives?

Yes, four - none of which keeps both source addresses and container-name resolution, which is the combination a reverse proxy needs.

- port_handler=slirp4netns - documented in containers.conf as the source-address-preserving handler, but it applies when slirp4netns is the network. It does not apply to a netavark bridge inside the rootless netns.
- --network=pasta - preserves source addresses, but gives up the bridge and aardvark-dns name resolution that a multi-container proxy setup depends on.
- --network=host for the proxy - works, but then every backend has to publish a port on the host loopback and service discovery by container name is lost.
- running the proxy rootful - works, but a rootful proxy cannot reach rootless containers, so in practice the whole stack has to move to rootful, which defeats the purpose of the rootless setup. 

### Additional context

comments.body:
Follow-up: pasta already has the missing piece. pasta -c <path> (EXPERIMENTAL) exposes a control socket, and pesto(1) can --add 
and --delete port forwardings on a running instance. That removes what I assumed was the blocker - that a shared per-netns pasta 
cannot be reconfigured as containers come and go.

So the shape could be: start pasta with -c instead of -t none -u none, and drive forwardings through the control socket on 
container start/stop, rather than spawning rootlessport?

I realise both --conf-path and pesto are marked EXPERIMENTAL, so this may be premature - but it does look like the pieces exist?

Hi team, I would like to work on this enhancement.

Currently in rootless mode with user-defined bridge networks, port forwarding uses host-level proxies which mask client source IP addresses. I can look into routing published port forwarding through pasta for user-defined networks to preserve incoming client source addresses, with integration tests.

Could you please assign this issue to me? Thanks!
+1 to this feature request, could be closely related to #28768 😄
This is already implemented in podman 6
